**Your fax numbers** is the landing page of the Partner Portal. Each row is a fax profile — a number, the license key that activates it in the customer's software, and its current state.

| Column | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Display name | How the number is labelled across the portal and on your carrier fax settings. Max 15 characters. |
| Fax number | The 10-digit number in service. |
| License key | The key the customer enters to activate fax. Masked by default — click the eye icon to reveal. |
| Date added | When the profile was provisioned. |
| Last activity | The most recent fax API event on this number. |

Use the search box to find a profile by name or number, and the **All / Active / Inactive / Pending** tabs to filter. If a port is in flight, a banner at the top of the page tells you how many numbers are on the way; they appear in this list automatically once the port completes.

<Frame caption="The fax profiles list, with search, status filters, and a banner for in-flight ports">
  ![The fax profiles list](data:image/jpeg;base64,)
</Frame>

## Managing a profile

Click the pencil icon on any row to open the profile drawer. It has three tabs.

### Settings

Rename the profile, and toggle **Active / Inactive** to start or pause fax delivery. The fax number itself is read-only.

The **Danger Zone** at the bottom holds **Remove fax profile**. Removing a profile is permanent — the license key stops working immediately and cannot be restored. If you only need to pause a customer, deactivate instead.

<Frame caption="Settings tab: display name, status toggle, and the Danger Zone">
  ![Settings tab](data:image/jpeg;base64,)
</Frame>

### Activity

A live feed of fax API events on this number — queued faxes, their timestamps, and the destination number. Leave **Hide empty polls** checked to filter out routine status checks and see only real traffic. This is the fastest way to confirm whether a customer's send actually reached us.

<Frame caption="Activity tab: recent fax API events for a single number">
  ![Activity tab](data:image/jpeg;base64,)
</Frame>

### Access

Shows which members of your organization can use this number. To share access, invite teammates from the **Team** tab in Account Settings.

<Frame caption="Access tab: who in your organization can use the number">
  ![Access tab](data:image/jpeg;base64,)
</Frame>

<Tip>
  Rename profiles to something your team will recognize at a glance — the pharmacy name usually beats the number.
</Tip>

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Where do I find a customer's license key?">
    On the fax profiles list, click the eye icon in the License Key column to reveal it. Keys are masked by default so they aren't exposed on a shared screen.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A customer says faxes aren't sending. What do I check first?">
    Open the profile, confirm the status toggle is **Active**, then check the **Activity** tab for queued events on that number. If nothing appears there, the send never reached us — look at the customer's software configuration and license key before escalating.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Should I deactivate or remove a profile?">
    Deactivate for anything temporary — a customer pausing service, a billing hold, a number you may bring back. Removal is permanent and the license key stops working immediately.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Why is the fax number field greyed out?">
    Numbers can't be edited after provisioning. If a customer needs a different number, provision a new profile or submit a port request.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="A number I ported isn't showing up.">
    Ported numbers appear here automatically once the port completes. Until then they sit under **Pending** and on the Port Status page.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How do I give a teammate access?">
    Invite them from the **Team** tab in Account Settings; the Access tab on each profile shows who currently has it.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
